Thin Clients Overview

1. What is a Thin Client?
  • A thin client connects to the Ignite cluster over a lightweight TCP protocol on port 10800;
  • Unlike a client node, a thin client does not join the cluster topology — no discovery overhead, no ring membership;
  • Thin clients have a much smaller footprint and faster startup;
2. Thin Client vs. Client Node
AspectThin ClientClient Node
ProtocolLightweight TCP binaryFull Ignite protocol
Joins topologyNoYes
Discovery overheadNoneFull discovery protocol
Startup timeFast (milliseconds)Slower (seconds)
Memory footprintSmallLarge (full Ignite instance)
Key-Value APIYesYes
SQLYesYes
ComputeYes (since 2.16)Yes
Continuous queriesYesYes
TransactionsYesYes
Near cacheNoYes
LanguagesJava, .NET, C++, Python, Node.JS, PHPJava, .NET, C++
3. When to use Thin Client vs. Client Node
  • Use thin client when:
    • You need a lightweight connection (microservices, serverless, short-lived processes);
    • You need non-Java access (Python, Node.JS, PHP);
    • You have many client connections (thin clients scale better);
  • Use client node when:
    • You need near cache support;
    • You need full event subscription capabilities;
    • You need to run collocated compute directly;
4. Partition Awareness
  • By default, thin clients send all requests to a single server node, which then routes to the correct partition owner;
  • Partition-aware thin clients learn the partition map and route requests directly to the node that owns the data — eliminating the extra hop: 
    ClientConfiguration cfg = new ClientConfiguration()
    .setAddresses("192.168.1.10:10800", "192.168.1.11:10800")
    .setPartitionAwarenessEnabled(true);

IgniteClient client = Ignition.startClient(cfg);
  • Partition awareness significantly improves read/write latency;
